prompt:
$$36x^{2}+kx+49=0$$

In the equation above, $k$ is a constant. For which of the following values of $k$ will the equation have more than one real solution?
explanation: Choice A is correct. A quadratic equation has more than one real solution when its discriminant is positive. For $36x^{2}+kx+49=0$, the discriminant is $k^{2}-4(36)(49)=k^{2}-7056$. Setting $k^{2}-7056>0$ gives $k^{2}>7056$, so $|k|>84$. This means $k<-84$ or $k>84$. Of the choices, only $-95<-84$ satisfies this condition.
